facts.statement: Alioramus had 76 or 78 teeth, a higher count than any other tyrannosaurid.

facts.statement: Alioramus possessed a locking mechanism in its lower jaw similar to Tarbosaurus, reducing flexibility compared to other tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: As in Tarbosaurus, a ridge on the outer surface of the angular bone of the lower jaw articulated with the rear of the dentary bone, locking the two bones together and removing much of the flexibility seen in other tyrannosaurids

facts.statement: A 2003 analysis classified Alioramus within the family Tyrannosauridae and subfamily Tyrannosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2004 study suggested Alioramus might belong outside the family Tyrannosauridae, reflecting a more basal position within Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: The description of Qianzhousaurus in 2014 established the tribe Alioramini, which includes Alioramus.

facts.statement: A second analysis found Alioramini to be the sister group of Tyrannosauridae, outside the clade including Albertosaurinae and Tyrannosaurinae.

facts.statement: However, more prominent nasal crests and a higher number of teeth suggest Alioramus is a separate genus, even if it is juvenile.
